portAndProcess.description: Verify what is actually listening where
checks: expectedPort responds and matches the project this checklist is for
process name/path at that port matches expected binary/entrypoint
no port collision with unrelated services (e.g. two projects both claiming 3000)

routeRegistration.description: Verify API routes actually exist on the running server
checks: each documented route returns non-404 on a basic request
route file on disk matches route path claimed in frontend fetch calls
base path / prefix (e.g. /api/v1) matches what frontend expects

requestResponseIntegrity.description: Verify write and read paths agree
checks: POST/write endpoint persists to a store
GET/read endpoint used by polling reads from the same store
no divergence between multiple routes writing to different backends for the same data

frontendBackendSync.description: Catch mismatches between UI code and server code
checks: no orphaned JS (missing function wrappers, syntax errors) — validate before deploy
API base URLs in frontend match actual server host/port
CORS config allows frontend origin if different from API origin

reviewCadence.description: How often and when this checklist gets re-verified
checks: re-scan ports/routes after any deploy or restart
periodic passive scan on an interval (default: every 30 min during active work sessions)
always re-verify immediately after a reported bug like 'X isn't working'

logicVerification.description: Review and verify Pete's proposed logic/structure before implementing, confirm status, and report back
checks: restate the proposed structure/logic in plain terms before building anything
confirm whether it's sound as-is, or flag gaps/risks
explicitly mark each review as RESOLVED (logic confirmed correct, proceeding as specified) or UNRESOLVED (logic has a gap — do not proceed until clarified)
report resolved/unresolved status back to Pete before or alongside implementation, not buried in unrelated output
